title: Unit 3 Stoichiometry Test
subject: chemistry
variation_policy: Preserve the exact 7-question constructed-response stoichiometry layout and mark emphasis while changing compounds, values, and contexts.

section_plans.title: Foundational Stoichiometry Calculations
section_plans.instructions: Show all work. Include units and use appropriate significant digits.

prebuilt_questions.stem: Calculate the amount of substance in moles for 7.22 x 10^23 formula units of zinc phosphate, Zn3(PO4)2(s).
Calculate the mass of 0.415 mol of aluminum sulfate, Al2(SO4)3(s).
How many hydrogen atoms are present in 0.750 mol of ammonia, NH3(g)?

section_plans.title: Composition and Reaction Stoichiometry
section_plans.instructions: Show a complete stoichiometric setup. Write and balance any required chemical equation before solving.

prebuilt_questions.stem: A compound is 52.2% carbon, 13.1% hydrogen, and 34.7% oxygen by mass. Its molar mass is 92.1 g/mol. Determine the molecular formula of the compound.
prebuilt_questions.answer_hint: Empirical formula C2H6O; molecular formula C4H12O2

prebuilt_questions.stem: In excess chlorine gas, iron reacts to form iron(III) chloride. Calculate the mass of FeCl3(s) produced when 11.2 g of iron is used.

Phosphoric acid reacts with calcium hydroxide to produce calcium phosphate and water. If 6.50 g of H3PO4(aq) reacts completely with excess Ca(OH)2(aq), what mass of Ca3(PO4)2(s) is produced? Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction.

section_plans.title: Lab Yield Analysis
section_plans.instructions: Use the data provided to determine theoretical yield and percent yield. Show your setup clearly.

prebuilt_questions.stem: Use the lab data below to determine the percentage yield of silver chloride, AgCl(s), produced when excess sodium chloride is added to silver nitrate solution. Lab data: mass of AgNO3 used = 1.62 g; mass of clean, dry filter paper = 1.14 g; mass of dry precipitate and filter paper = 2.48 g. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
prebuilt_questions.answer_hint: AgNO3 + NaCl -> AgCl + NaNO3; actual precipitate mass = 1.34 g; theoretical yield is about 1.37 g AgCl; percentage yield is about 98.0%

generation_constraints: Generate exactly 7 constructed-response questions across the three sections.
Include at least one formula-units or particles to moles conversion.
Include at least one moles-to-mass calculation.
Include at least one atoms or particles counting question.
Include at least one balanced-equation stoichiometry problem that asks for a product mass or amount.
Include one percent-yield lab problem based on measured precipitate data.
